input.note: First 33 probes of the 64-probe / 25258-token sealed corpus. Layers 0-2 DeltaNet, layer 3 GQA. Same input used for before and after.

profile_first.algorithm: unmodified compute (legacy 4-worker MoE clamp, per-token DeltaNet gemv_bf16 re-widen, per-f32 write_all)

diagnosis.primary_hypothesis_worker_clamp: REFUTED as the dominant cost. Routed-expert wave is 1.84% of compute at 4719 tokens with the stale 4-worker cap.
actual_hot_paths: retention_flush 48.9%: write_retained_hidden_f32le issued 2048 write_all(4-byte) syscalls per row (18848 rows).
mixer 48.4%: DeltaNet gemv_bf16 re-widened QKVZ (12288x2048, 50 MiB) and out_proj on every token. GQA already widened once (layer 3 was 27.8s vs ~50s DeltaNet layers).

clamp_sweep_one_layer.finding: Raising the clamp from 4 to 28 oversubscribed Accelerate M=1 GEMVs and slowed the expert wave (3.3s -> 12.2s over 4 layers). 8 workers is the measured sweet spot. Memory headroom was never the binding constraint at this corpus size.

applied: Coalesce hidden-row writes to one LE buffer + one write_all; parallelize flush across up to 16 threads.
Widen DeltaNet QKVZ and out_proj once per layer (matches large-mat gemv_bf16 = gemm_bf16 path). BA stays on-the-fly convert (below widen threshold).
Parallelize mixer across probes (DeltaNet uses available cores; GQA capped at 4 so Accelerate can own long sgemm).
Replace the stale 2/4/8 token-count ladder with a memory-aware cap defaulting to 8 workers (measured).
did_not_pay: Raising MoE workers to 20-28: RSS stayed under 16 GiB but expert-wave wall got worse (AMX oversubscription). Negative result on the primary clamp hypothesis as a speed lever.
not_attempted: Metal expert wave. CPU levers delivered 4.4x; GPU remains a separate step.
